hazards.name: Lack of street lighting
hazards.description: No visible street light poles, which may reduce pedestrian visibility and safety during nighttime hours.

hazards.name: Wide, straight roadway
hazards.description: The wide, straight nature of the road without visible traffic calming may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Narrow Walkway
hazards.description: The existing sidewalk on the right is very narrow and lacks a buffer from moving traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image adjacent to the brick buildings

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals visible for a long stretch of residential frontage, forcing unsafe mid-block crossings.

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Design
hazards.description: The wide, straight lanes with minimal roadside friction and no traffic calming encourage high vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Unmarked wide crossing
hazards.description: The wide, straight roadway lacks marked crossings, which can encourage higher vehicle speeds and increase risk for pedestrians crossing to the church.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Mature trees on the right side of the street may block the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of mid-block crossing
hazards.description: In a residential area with mature trees and fences, the absence of a designated crossing point may encourage unsafe mid-block crossings if intersections are far apart.

hazards.name: Wide travel lanes
hazards.description: The width of the travel lanes and the lack of traffic calming may encourage vehicle speeds that exceed safe limits for a residential area.

hazards.name: Lack of immediate roadside walkway
hazards.description: Pedestrians wishing to walk directly alongside the road have no paved surface, though a setback sidewalk exists.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalks
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible, forcing pedestrians to cross the wide street without protection or priority.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the visible stretch of the road.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection Crossing
hazards.description: The lack of marked crosswalks at the junction increases the risk for pedestrians crossing the street as their right-of-way is not clearly defined.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image at the road junction

hazards.name: Potential for high vehicle speeds
hazards.description: The wide, straight roadway with minimal traffic calming may encourage speeds higher than appropriate for a residential street.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility paint to designate safe crossing points and alert drivers to pedestrian presence.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repair and repave the sidewalk to provide a level, ADA-compliant walking surface free of vegetation.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or street trees to create a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation and Definition
interventions.description: Use curbing or bollards to define a specific, narrow vehicle access point for the lot on the right, reducing the pedestrian conflict area.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct continuous, ADA-compliant paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks and compliant curb ramps at the intersection to provide a designated and safer crossing point.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing/Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the width of travel lanes or repurpose excess pavement to slow traffic and reduce the pedestrian crossing distance.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing with Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with a central refuge island to break up the crossing distance and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or raised crosswalks to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential context.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Infill
interventions.description: Construct a continuous paved sidewalk on the left side of the street to ensure a safe, dedicated path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Raised Curbs
interventions.description: Install raised curbs to provide physical separation between the roadway and the sidewalk, preventing vehicle encroachment.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add high-visibility crosswalks and pedestrian signage to designate safe crossing points.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Replace the degraded pavement with a smooth, continuous concrete sidewalk to eliminate tripping hazards.

interventions.title: Vertical Curb Installation
interventions.description: Install a standard 6-inch vertical curb to provide physical and psychological separation between pedestrians and motor vehicles.
